name: refactor_kotlin_currency_formatters_to_shared_function
description: Collapses three copy-pasted currency formatters (formatUsd/formatEur/formatGbp, identical logic apart from the symbol) into one formatMoney(cents, symbol) function, keeping the three original names as thin wrappers; behavior-drift broken puts the negative sign AFTER the symbol instead of before it
prompts: Money.kt defines formatUsd, formatEur, and formatGbp - three functions with IDENTICAL cents-to-string formatting logic, differing only in which currency symbol they use. Refactor this into one shared function `formatMoney(cents: Int, symbol: String): String` holding the one copy of the logic (sign handling, symbol, decimal places), and reimplement formatUsd/formatEur/formatGbp as one-line wrappers calling it with their respective symbol. Preserve the exact existing output format for all three, including that a negative amount's '-' sign comes BEFORE the currency symbol (e.g. -500 cents in USD is "-$5.00", not "$-5.00").

reference_solution.src/main/kotlin/com/optarena/app/Money.k:
package com.optarena.app

fun formatMoney(cents: Int, symbol: String): String {
    val sign = if (cents < 0) "-" else ""
    val c = kotlin.math.abs(cents)
    return "$sign$symbol${c / 100}.${(c % 100).toString().padStart(2, '0')}"
}

fun formatUsd(cents: Int): String = formatMoney(cents, "$")
fun formatEur(cents: Int): String = formatMoney(cents, "€")
fun formatGbp(cents: Int): String = formatMoney(cents, "£")
